data_source: PUBLIC PLACEHOLDER — NOT THE USER'S OWN DATA. Fitted to PhysioNet MIT-BIH Normal Sinus Rhythm Database (nsrdb) record 16265, a 32-year-old male, 22.24 h of annotated beat-to-beat intervals starting at clock time 08:04. The user's Apple Health export was not present on this machine (~/Downloads and ~/Documents searched); digitaltwin/signals/apple_health.py is ready to ingest it, after which this parameter set must be refitted and is_user_personal_data set to true.

rules: both bounding annotations must be normal sinus beats ('N')

heart_rate.resting_hr_definition: mean of the lowest decile of 5-min window mean HR (27 of 267 windows)
heart_rate.hr_max_age_predicted_note: Tanaka 2001 (208 - 0.7*age, age 32) — PREDICTED, not measured; no graded exercise test exists for this record
heart_rate.hr_reserve_caveat: A 24 h ambulatory recording contains no maximal effort; the observed-basis reserve is a lower bound and the predicted-basis reserve rests on a population regression, not on this subject.

hrv_bands_hz.spectral_method: Lomb-Scargle periodogram on the unevenly sampled NN series; PSD normalisation verified against a sinusoid of known amplitude (recovered/expected = 1.000)

hr_equivalent.note: HR-space cosinor fitted on the first 18 h only (design A training set)

circadian.coverage_caveat: 22.24 h of a 24 h cycle; clock hour 07 is unobserved, so the circadian term is interpolated there.

rr_model.data_source: PhysioNet MIT-BIH Normal Sinus Rhythm Database (nsrdb) record 16265 (32 M, 22.24 h) — PUBLIC PLACEHOLDER, NOT THE USER'S OWN DATA

rr_model_note: Deliverable parameter set, fitted on all 99,658 NN intervals. Interface: digitaltwin.signals.rr_generator.RRGenerator.generate(duration_s, state='rest'|'active'|'mixed', seed=, start_clock_h=).

design_A_temporal_extrapolation.definition: params fitted on first 18.00 h; held-out last 4.24 h (clock 02:07-06:31)
design_A_temporal_extrapolation.verdict: FAILS. Mean HR +17.3% (70.8 vs 60.4 bpm), KS D=0.611. A single 24 h cosinor fitted on an 18 h window cannot extrapolate into clock hours it never saw; RMSSD -37%, pNN50 -50%.

fitted_params.data_source: PhysioNet MIT-BIH Normal Sinus Rhythm Database (nsrdb) record 16265 (32 M, 22.24 h) — PUBLIC PLACEHOLDER, NOT THE USER'S OWN DATA

design_B_interleaved_blocks.definition: 26 of 134 non-overlapping 10-min blocks withheld at random (seed 7, 19.7% of beats); circadian term interpolates
design_B_interleaved_blocks.verdict: PASSES on rate and short-term variability, over-disperses on SDNN. Block-median comparisons: mean HR +5.0%, HR p05/p50/p95 within 7%, LF +5.1%, RMSSD -13.2%, pNN50 -11.0%, DFA alpha1 -0.8%, HF +29.9%, LF/HF -31.1%, SDNN +33.0%, spectral slope -1.097 vs -0.882 (abs diff -0.215). KS D=0.077 on the pooled HR distribution.

fitted_params.data_source: PhysioNet MIT-BIH Normal Sinus Rhythm Database (nsrdb) record 16265 (32 M, 22.24 h) — PUBLIC PLACEHOLDER, NOT THE USER'S OWN DATA

validation.known_deficiency: The single-slope power law fitted over [1e-3, 0.15] Hz is steeper than the in-block behaviour, over-predicting sub-0.04 Hz variance; this inflates 10-min block SDNN by ~33% and is the model's main residual error. A two-slope (broken power law) 1/f term would address it but is outside the generative structure specified for this model.
validation.ks_note: With n ~ 2x10^4 beats a KS p-value is uninformative; the D statistic is the effect size to read.

apple_health_parser.tests: tests/test_apple_health.py — 11/11 passed on a synthetic export (XML, zip, ECG CSV)

sources: PhysioNet MIT-BIH Normal Sinus Rhythm Database (PMID 10851218 / doi:10.13026/C2NK5R); Task Force ESC/NASPE 1996 HRV standards (PMID 8598068); Tanaka 2001 HRmax equation (PMID 11153730)
